harness.name: VVAH
harness.description: Visa Vulnerability Agentic Harness (vvaharness 1.5.1). A Python pipeline: stages S0-S11, typed config, model calls wrapped by deterministic code.

components.doc: Package root: resolves __version__ and lazily exposes the embeddable API (remediate, validate).
`python -m vvaharness` entry: delegates to the CLI main and exits with its code.
Packaged operating instructions for AI coding agents (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md skill, GEMINI.md). Written by `vvaharness setup --install-agents`; tells an agent to OPERATE the tool, not edit it.
The embeddable surface: remediate(finding) -> Remediation; validate(finding, remediation) -> Verdict.
Public surface of the harness family: re-exports the contract (vocabularies, options, messages, errors), the permission gate, provider routing and the backend registry. Consumers import from here.
Backend traits a host (S10/S11 only) must know before building a prompt, keyed by the `via` selector. Never consulted for a detection prompt.

ClaudeHarness: the Claude Agent SDK (cli/sdk via) implementation of Harness. One-shot and streaming sessions, persona-report collection (submit tool first, transcript scrape as fallback), whole-session deadline with interrupt + grace drain.

S11's fact tools and report channel for the Claude-harness route, exposed as an in-process MCP server ("facts"): tools arrive as mcp__facts__X; SubmitPersonaReport validates a persona's report on submission.
The Claude backend's SDK-to-harness exception mapping. ProcessError is absent by design (wrap_sdk_error copies its exit code and stderr tail itself).

Translate harness option dataclasses into ClaudeAgentOptions: env pins, verbatim prompts, tool policy, permission callback, structured-output schema, the in-process fact MCP server, subagents and the foreground-dispatch hook that keeps persona subagents blocking.
Claude Agent SDK message -> HarnessMessage translation; the terminal ResultMessage feeds the process-wide token/cost counter exactly once per session.
Re-export of the harness exception hierarchy defined in harness.models. Never defines a class: a copy would compare by identity and void the VVAH-E001/E002 halt guards.
DeepAgents backend package: resolves DeepAgentHarness lazily (PEP 562) so unrelated imports skip deepagents.

DeepAgentHarness: the deepagents/LangGraph agent loop an S4 session runs on. Shows how the session's graph is built (model, system prompt + suffixes, tools, skills, middleware stack, recursion limit) and how the stream is bounded by the session timeout and the recursion limit. Short summary; retry/transport-fallback arms condensed.

Middleware that rejects a session's structured verdict until every todo on its plan is completed (and, when required_tools is set, a graph tool has been called). Relents after max_rejections and lets the verdict through.
Middleware that withholds a fixed set of tools from every model request (un-advertises only; a forged call to a withheld tool would still run -- PermitTools is the fail-closed gate).

ForceVerdictOnly middleware: leaves tool_choice on auto while a session works; when the model stops without reporting, re-issues the call with only the outcome tool, forced. Installed only when force_verdict_only is set (S10 validation launcher and the remediation plugin runner); S4 sessions do not install it.

Middleware that repairs a tool call langchain could not parse as JSON: the call is moved into tool_calls with args={} and paired with an error ToolMessage, so the model sees the failure instead of the session breaking. request.override touches only the outgoing request, so the same unrepaired call recurs; counting dedupes by id.

Loop-budget constants for the DeepAgents backend. max_turns is a FLOOR on the LangGraph recursion limit (max_turns + headroom supersteps, ~2*turns+3 nodes per turn), not a turn cap; sdk/cli enforce it as a hard cap.

ModelCallBudget middleware: caps model calls per session; on the last permitted call every tool but the outcome tool is withdrawn and a FINAL TURN notice is appended. S4 opts in to raising VVAH-E007 if even that forced turn does not end the session.

The DeepAgents backend's data contract: TLS/credential env keys, the model cache key, the filesystem deny rules (read-only sessions, .git internals), the native tool inventory, subagent and graph shapes.

Public surface of the deepagents options package (model, graph and subagent-spec builders), plus the import-time registration of the "openai" provider profile used by bare-string models that skip build_model.

Filesystem permissioning, backend selection and skill sources for deepagents sessions: write-deny globs, a no-write backend, a path jail, a scan-scope-confined read backend (read/grep/glob/ls filtered to the S1 inventory), an optional executing shell backend, a .git-guarded stock backend, and grep/glob timeout patching.

ForcingChatAnthropic: restores the forced tool_choice that langchain_anthropic drops under ADAPTIVE thinking (the API allows it there), so S2/S4/S6 sessions cannot end on prose and lose their structured output.
LangGraph invoke-config construction: a fresh random thread id and, when max_turns is set, a recursion limit of max_turns + buffer (LangGraph counts supersteps, not turns).

Resolves a model id to a chat model (Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible) with timeout, retries, output ceiling and reasoning/thinking settings; also owns the REASON_IN_PROMPT suffix used when think_in_prompt replaces native reasoning. (TLS/proxy/client-injection plumbing omitted.)

One-shot (single-turn parser) graph compilation: which native tools are advertised vs. permitted to execute (fail closed via PermitTools; the subagent dispatch "task" never permitted), redaction on read-only, cache/suffix tweaks.

Structured-output strategy: forced tool-calling (ToolStrategy) on Anthropic unless the model rejects forcing; a textual submit instruction is appended to the system prompt whenever forcing is dropped or unsupported.

Subagent tool resolution and native DeepAgents subagent specs (one per persona + a gated general-purpose spec that shadows deepagents' ungated, unredacted builtin), each with its own middleware stack.

ToolCallStateChatOpenAI (Chat Completions only): captures per-tool-call fields an endpoint put outside the OpenAI schema and sends them back on the same call when the conversation is replayed (avoids VVAH-E006 rejections).
Executor-side gate: refuses any tool call whose name is not in the permitted set (FAILS CLOSED, logs names only). ExcludeTools only un-advertises; this blocks forged calls too.

Harness profiles for OpenAI-compatible models: the "investigation floor" system-prompt suffix registered with deepagents per provider (openai only) and per stage-keyed model. Anthropic routes get no suffix.

Anthropic prompt caching via block-level cache_control markers only (some proxies DROP the stock middleware's top-level cache_control): marks system, tools and, on agentic sessions, the conversation tail.

Read-only session middleware: mask PII/credentials in content-returning native tool results (read_file, grep), elide non-text blocks, and withhold the write tools + delete. Deny rules FAIL OPEN, so writes are also withheld.

ToolCallBudget middleware: caps how many times one session may call a named (metered) set of tools, refuses the over-budget call, then withdraws the tool family from the tool list with a one-time notice.

Anthropic models that reject a forced tool_choice with a 400: classified from the error, learned process-wide, and seeded with known rejecters so S10/S11 skip the first failed call (callers then retry without forcing).

Logical -> native tool-name resolution for the DeepAgents backend, the session-tool permit set (fails closed on native-name collisions) and build_tools (returns no tools: natives come from the filesystem middleware).
Translate DeepAgents / LangGraph state and stream events into HarnessMessage types: final text, structured response (wins over an earlier refusal), truncation and refusal flags, token usage.
Recover token usage for DeepAgents sessions from AIMessage usage_metadata, normalized to fresh input (input_tokens - cache_read - cache_creation), with a per-persona (subagent namespace) breakdown.
Abstract Harness contract every agent runtime (ClaudeHarness, DeepAgentHarness) implements.

The harness family's data contract: the logical/native tool vocabularies that the permission gates read, effort/provider enums, session/one-shot/streaming options, streamed message types and the VVAH-E00x errors.

Write-permission predicate used by PermissionsPolicy: Write is allowed only to a permitted output file sitting directly in the target directory. No command-parsing predicates (Bash is denied outright).

PermissionsPolicy: the deny-by-default permission gate for a validation (S11) session. Tool names come from the vocabulary in harness.models. TRAP: the SDK skips can_use_tool for bare-listed tools, so listing "Write" in allowed_tools would void evaluate_write.
Which vendor a (model, provider) pair resolves to, and the credential env overrides for that vendor. Must not import deepagents/langchain/anthropic/openai (preflight and manifest rely on that).
Backend registry: maps the `via` selector to a lazy Harness factory (each backend's SDK imported only on use).

Repeated-identical-tool-call guard (VVAH-E009) wrapped around the S10 validation and remediation stream consumers. S4 sessions are not wrapped by it (S4 relies on tool/model-call budgets and the recursion limit).
Append one streaming session's messages to a JSONL transcript. Silently inert unless VVAHARNESS_TRANSCRIPT_DIR is set; a transcript failure never breaks the scan.
LLM backend package marker: no logic. Kept as a regular package so it beats a leftover backends/llm.py module (shipped through 1.2.0) in site-packages.

Claude Agent SDK backend for the Remediation Agent's fix mode (via: sdk with mutation tools; sdk.py itself is read-only). Deny-by-default PreToolUse gate: Read/Glob/Grep allowed, Edit/Write confined to cwd (no symlinks, no .git), Bash denied.
Prompt-cache policy shared by the cli/sdk/openai backends: which caching mechanism a route uses, whether cache_markers permits markers, and reporting of cache usage keys the parser does not cover.

The `claude` CLI backend namespace that registry.py resolves for via: cli. Pure re-exports of the cli/* submodules (cancel, discovery, env, envelope, oneshot, process, retry, session); no logic of its own.
Ctrl-C propagation for the cli route: a process-global abort flag, the live `claude` process registry, out-of-band abort hooks, and the process-tree kill / graceful stop.
Locating the `claude` binary (no cwd-planted hits), probing which flags the installed build accepts (memoised), mapping permission modes to a safe accepted one, and formatting CLI errors.
Process-global cli config (TLS, proxy, effort, restricted) and the per-call `claude` subprocess env: Node TLS env vars, the effort pin, refusal-resend disable, and the output-token cap.
Reading the `claude --output-format json` envelope (one dict, a list, or NDJSON): canned-guardrail detection, typed refusals, usage/spend/telemetry, structured_output, and split-reply stitching.

via: cli prompt() -- one request, one reply, no tools: `claude -p --tools ""` with the JSON envelope, probe-gated --json-schema/--max-budget-usd, one doubled-budget truncation retry, refusal and quality gates.

Running the `claude` subprocess, buffered (with heartbeat) or streaming (line callback + turn watchdog); registers the process for Ctrl-C, stops it gracefully on timeout, and renders --verbose traces.

The cli retry policy around one `claude` subprocess: rate-limit/overload backoff, bounded timeout retry, auth (VVAH-E001) short retries, proxy/TLS (VVAH-E002) fail-fast, refusal first, truncation (VVAH-E005) helpers.
via: cli agentic session (the `claude` subprocess): turn watchdog, wall-clock kill, and a tool-less resume of the killed session that asks for its final answer.

In-process SDK-MCP bridge for via: cli with caller tools (cli.mcp_tools): the pinned `claude` binary runs through the Agent SDK with the stage's graph/CWE fact tools as mcp__vvah_facts__*; deny-by-default PreToolUse read jail (no --restricted).
via: deepagents -- LangGraph harness route: options assembly, transient retry ladder, refusal/auth/proxy classification. max_turns here is a recursion limit, not a hard turn cap as on sdk/cli/openai.
Shared backend vocabulary: the structured-output tool, its re-ask and submit-instruction prompt lines, effort-scaled clocks and the refusal/truncation taxonomy used by every route.

via: openai -- OpenAI-compatible chat/responses loop with read-only localtools (no Edit/Write: fix mode errors). Hard turn cap, one prose re-ask, then a forced-final call that keeps only the submit tool when a schema is forced.

Pure Chat <-> Responses API translation for the openai route (no I/O): the same Chat-shaped transcript replays over either wire; private keys carry Responses-only replay state (encrypted reasoning, function_call item ids).

Backend dispatcher: every stage calls prompt()/agentic() here; a model node (id, via, provider, extras) picks the route. Also holds the per-role model routing table and the route-wide transport/cache/refusal/pricing settings.
via: sdk -- raw Anthropic Messages loop with read-only localtools; mutating/Bash tool requests are delegated to the Claude Agent SDK. Hard turn cap, one prose re-ask, then a forced final answer.
Shared TLS-config coercion, Anthropic auth kwargs (static key vs OAuth token) and mTLS client-chain handling for the backend clients. Stdlib only; warnings carry no file contents.
In-process langchain-tool adapter: carries a stage's caller fact tools (graph, CweGuidance) onto the via: sdk / via: openai raw loops, honouring the caller's budget and EvidenceGate middleware.

Sandboxed read-only Read/Glob/Grep ("localtools") for the non-CLI raw loops (sdk.py, openai.py): jailed to cwd and to the S1 inventory once set_scope() is called; binary/data-URI elision, size caps, redaction of content.

vvaharness CLI entry point: loads .env, strips logging flags, prints help, and dispatches to the subcommands (setup, doctor, estimate, gc, remediate, ev-replay, validate) or to scan under the run manifest.
The Typer application: command names and help; each command forwards its untouched argv to the existing hand-rolled dispatcher (VvaharnessCli.dispatch) and surfaces its exit code.
The non-scan subcommand handlers: doctor (readiness + live probe), estimate (offline scope preview), gc (state DB pruning), validate (S11), remediate (S10 from a prior scan), ev-replay.

Selection and loading of a trusted .env from exactly cwd or home (never an ancestor, never inside the scan target unless VVAHARNESS_ALLOW_CWD_CONFIG is set); values never override the existing environment.
Config/repo path resolution from raw argv and the config trust boundary shared by every subcommand.
Readiness wizard plus opt-in env-file/instruction installation. Preserve filesystem guards and all write conditions.
The context-graph-sdk boundary: one workspace, one graph, per scan. Facade re-exporting build_graph, GraphHandle and the deterministic graph queries. No logic of its own.

S0: builds the one code graph a scan analyses (context-graph-sdk Workspace on an ArcadeDB backend, plus enrichers), and the degenerate-graph test that decides whether graph-evidence demands can be enforced.
The live graph handle a scan carries from S0 to the last stage that queries the graph; owns the workspace.
S1: deterministic ContextPackage fields from the built graph via Cypher: modules (communities -> files), primary language, and a one-line system-context note.
Read-only graph-query tools over ctx.graph_handle; S2, S4 and S6 each build these. Tool docstrings are the descriptions the model sees; error results carry hints instead of raising.

Config loading overview: profile YAML (the operator's --config, ./config.yaml or a packaged profile) deep-merged over built-in step defaults, then an optional trusted config.local.yaml overlay, then ${VAR} expansion. Knobs are read where they act.

Regex matching of a MatchSpec corpus against raw source text: line-by-line seeding (S0 sources/sinks) and detector rules whose gates read a call/block span, a widened negative window, a file gate and a proximity gate.
The default source/sink corpus S0 matches against source text, plus the declarative S5 detector rules. Every callee is a public, documented API defensible from CWE semantics; never benchmark-led.
S0: turns matcher hits into typed Sink and EntryPoint records for the seed package.
MatchSpec: one compiled pattern a static detector treats as a source, sink, or detector rule, plus the gate fields a detector rule uses to decide whether a line hit fires.
Package facade for the deterministic S2 threat-model evidence: re-exports gather(), the per-kind gatherers, the capped reader and the block renderers. No logic of its own.
Breadth-before-depth selection shared by manifest and config-rep discovery: one item per group per round, so every group is represented before any group gets a second item.
S2 evidence: API-contract artefacts (OpenAPI/Swagger/Protobuf/GraphQL/WSDL/Avro/Thrift/META-INF/AndroidManifest), paths only.
S2 evidence: representative config files, one per directory (security-named first, then env tier), with redacted, capped bodies for the first few and path-only for the rest.
S2 evidence: README/SECURITY/ARCHITECTURE-shaped documents within a shared char budget: fixed-name docs breadth-first, then grow truncated ones, then a few name-matched extra .md/.rst files.

S2 deterministic (no-LLM) threat-model evidence snapshot: resolves the step2.* caps, samples the AST frontier, gathers docs/manifests/config reps/API artefacts, and truncates prompt lists, counting every cut.
S2 evidence: build/dependency manifests found by a depth-bounded walk, structurally truncated to their dependency sections, round-robin across kinds, then under an aggregate char cap.
The containment-checked, length-capped chokepoint every S2 evidence read from disk goes through.
ThreatEvidence -> prompt-ready text blocks for the S2 threat-model prompt.
Stub for S6 live exploit verification (out of scope): holds only its config knobs. Prompts, payloads and attack logic are deliberately not rendered.
Loads the known-CVE feed (inject.cve_file) as prioritisation context. Missing file -> empty; malformed structure -> empty with a warning; a malformed record drops only itself.
Loads design controls (auth boundaries, sandboxes, mitigations) from YAML (inject.controls_file). Missing file -> empty; any parse or validation error -> the whole list is empty (all-or-nothing).
Classifies a repo's files by language (extension map, then path/content sniffing for IaC, CI, Ansible, Kubernetes and mainframe sources) and tells source apart from config and templates.

Run-level scan manifest: tool version, model roles (with resolved route/transport/effort), config hashes, effective scan controls, target git SHA, timing, per-stage telemetry, errors, S11 rollup and counters.
Re-export hub for the data contracts passed between pipeline steps (no raw dicts cross steps).
FindingCase: the per-finding record S10 and S11 both write; `state` is derived from the attempts, never stored.
ScoringPolicy: the gate set a validator owes and how the host bands its score into merge readiness.
Pure decisions computed from a case: case state from attempts, merge readiness from a verdict.
One named check (gate), its outcome and the source evidence cited for it; shared by S10 and S11.
Provenance: who produced a remediation/verdict, with what model and backend, at what cost. Never holds credentials.

Remediation contract: what an S10 engine produced; finalize() turns engine evidence into the contract. The pydantic model Remediation is rendered as record RemediationData; class Remediation holds finalize().
Re-export hub for the scan data contracts (coercion helpers, render helpers, findings, threat model, work units, metrics, report).
Lenient coercion helpers used by model validators to absorb off-schema LLM output instead of rejecting it.
Renders one ranked finding's Markdown report section as (line, in_sarif_description) pairs, including CVSS/VSVS/offensive-priority lines, dedup duplicates and the exploit-verification block.
Markdown-safety helpers shared by the report renderers: neutralise headings, fences, line breaks, invisible/bidi characters and HTML angles in untrusted (repo- or model-authored) text.
Report sections for exploit chains (S8 output), the unreachable-files appendix, the CMDB app profile and the threat-model section (ranked threats with per-threat investigation-unit disposition).
Report sections: Scan Metrics (tokens by phase, language LOC coverage), the Verification funnel (raw -> verified -> reported reconciliation), Scan Health warnings and the Scan Scope appendix.

Report helpers: the chunk-kind line of Scan Metrics and the Pipeline Diagnostics block, which turns non-default stage counters (truncation, caps, retries, unenforced evidence gates, clamps) into disclosures.

ContextPackage: what S1 emits (entry points, sinks, modules, files, injected CVEs/controls/CMDB, threat model), plus astContextView, the capped "frontier" view S2 evidence gathering builds its prompt from.
Findings and their post-processing forms: Finding, LinkEvidence (S8 per-hop schema the model fills; its field descriptions are prompt text), Chain, RankedFinding, DroppedFinding.
Externally injected contracts threaded through every step: CVEs, design controls, the CMDB app profile.

ScanMetrics: coverage, verification and token/cost stats plus the snapshot of every stage counter the report renders; ScopeEntry: one analysis unit (chunk) in the scope appendix. All counters default 0 so old payloads validate.

FinalReport: the findings.json shape S9 writes, its health predicates (hollow scan, undetermined drops, coverage loss, unranked split) and the Markdown renderer that assembles every report section in order.
SeedPackage: S0's deterministic seed (entry points, sinks, taint paths, languages, full walk), merged into S1's output.
Code-location contracts populated by S0/S1 and external scanners: EntryPoint, Sink, ModuleInfo.
The threat model S2 produces (assets, boundaries, threats): schema, off-schema enum coercion, and the deterministic rank + coverage-preserving caps S2.run applies.

The work units S3 emits: one InvestigationUnit per threat (with its validated file surface, sinks, entry points, CVEs, CWEs), the TaskManifest holding them, and DupLocation (a dedup-collapsed site kept on a finding).
Verdict (rendered as record FixVerdict; the name is taken elsewhere): one validator's conclusion about one remediation; Ticket: a deferred verdict handle.

Shared vocabulary: closed enums (Severity, VulnClass, RemediationKind/Outcome, Disposition, Decision, GateStatus, CaseState, MergeReadiness) with their lenient parsers, offensive-priority labels and gate-name lists.
Orchestrator package facade: re-exports the scan entry, batch runner, checkpoint helpers, config path helpers and preflight probes so callers (and tests) reach them as vvaharness.orchestrator.<name>.
Names of the directories a scan leaves in the target checkout, and the guard that refuses to write artifacts through a symlink, onto a non-directory, or outside the target tree.

Batch mode (--repo-file): parse the repo list, drop skip-pattern repos, clone each (or each app group) and run one OrchestratorScan per repo or per application, resetting process-global state between them.
Mints the stable content-addressed case_id each finding is tracked under (file, line bucket, CWE), so a re-scan that reports the same bug a few lines away keeps the same case directory.
Remediation/validation rollup for the run manifest: counts of case states and decisions only (cases live in the untrusted target, so no titles, paths or ids reach run_manifest).
Checkpoint/resume: step-key derivation and JSON (never pickle) storage of each stage's output in the SQLite state store, schema-validated on load so a tampered or stale blob re-runs the step instead.
CMDB lookup: resolves inject.cmdb_file and maps an application_id to an AppProfile (threaded into S1-S8) plus the raw AppInfo (used post-S7 for context severity).

Config file resolution and trust: default config lookup, refusal of a --config inside the scan target, UNC-safe path resolution, and the list of active model roles (used by preflight, doctor and the manifest).

Post-S7 enrichment: optional path prefixing (batch/monorepo), canonical CWE, vector-derived CVSS score and rating, CMDB-context VulContextSeverity score, and the offensive priority each verified finding carries into S8.
`vvaharness scan` CLI: flags, config trust gate + load, step1 overlay resolution, backend configuration, exploit-verification gates, preflight, then batch or single-repo scan with exit-code mapping.

The typed scan result (findings.json) written beside the Markdown report, redacted and atomically replaced, and read back strictly (absent -> null; present but invalid -> error, never a Markdown fallback).

Startup readiness: push transport/TLS/cache settings to the backend clients, check credentials per route, then live-probe every (model, via, provider) with a ping and the agentic roles with a forced tool round-trip.

L0 pipeline for one repository: pre-S1 exploit-verification prep, auto-exclude overlay, S0..S9, ingest upload, in-scan S10 remediation and S11 validation, each stage behind a checkpoint that --resume may replay. Resume rule: a stage reuses its checkpoint only when every upstream stage was itself restored (a re-run invalidates downstream).

State store facade: one SQLite file under $VVAHARNESS_STATE_DIR holding per-run checkpoint blobs, callgraph snapshots, exploit-verification replays/probes, and run metadata. Re-exports _db, callgraph, replays.

SQL schema of the state DB (runs, checkpoints, ev_replays, ev_probes, callgraph_* tables) and the v1->v2 (callgraph tables) and v2->v3 (ev tables) migrations. Rendered as records with their constraints.
Per-run entry-point and sink snapshots: an entry/sink qnode index (no edges) written as rows and bound to the stage that produced it, and read back as isolated call_graph nodes.
Exploit-verification replay bundles and probe logs, per run (storage only; EV logic is out of scope).

Bound a stage at a wall clock; when it expires, resume the pinned session (one extra user turn) or, failing that, re-ask a fresh tool-less call from the recorded transcript. Used by S2, S4, S6 and S8.

S0: deterministic source/sink text matching that seeds entry points and sinks (no model call). Also holds the degenerate-graph gate (codegraph/build.graph_is_degenerate) that step0.min_graph_nodes_for_gate drives.

S11: validate each S10 fix case with a 3-persona panel (one orchestrator session per case, personas as subagents), then synthesize persona gate reports on the host and score the fix. Cases run sequentially.

S1 auto-exclude: one model call proposes a per-target step1 exclusion overlay from a deterministic repo survey; deterministic vetoes (language erasure, templates, key material, secrets, client sinks, dedup widenings) and a scope gate then filter it.

S1: injects CVEs/controls, merges the S0 seed, and derives modules, notes and language from the graph. No model call. The repo walk (scope/walk.py) and config dedup (scope/configs.py) that the step1.* scope knobs drive are rendered here too.

S2 entry: the application threat model, reasoned over S1's mapped attack surface. gather evidence -> baseline block -> user prompt -> agentic call (one unforced resend) -> parse (one repair) -> finalize -> hollow retry -> baseline audit -> caps.
S2's minimum-baseline audit: which required baseline items a threat model left undisposed, and whether an undisposed item's category is still covered by some other threat's wording.
S2's reply parsing and the deterministic finalisation of its threats (ids by position, surface_files resolved to inventory).
S2's prompt text: the SYSTEM brief, the agentic/graph/shell system lines, the baseline block, the evidence-bearing user prompt, and the JSON repair re-ask.

S2's dispatch: the agentic threat-model session (graph tools, planning, evidence gate, call budget, deadline + resume/replay) and the tool-less hollow retry. Also the step2 evidence caps gather() reads.
S2's todo-list planning prompts (TodoListMiddleware system prompt + write_todos tool description). Installed by S2Session.threatmodelCall only when step2.planning is on and graph tools are mounted.

S3: builds the risk-ranked TaskManifest deterministically from S2's ThreatModel, one InvestigationUnit per threat. No model call; no catch-all unit for files no threat named (they are reported as unreachable).
Package marker for the S4 helpers (batching, outcomes, prompts, session). The real file holds only the license header; it defines nothing.
Groups S4 investigation units into shared sessions, preferring units whose files overlap. LARGE units always run alone.

S4's output contract (Pydantic schemas whose Field descriptions are prompt text the model sees) and the reducer from raw session replies to findings plus a per-unit verdict (confirmed/refuted/inconclusive, or failed/uninvestigated for a lost reply).

S4 prompts: one scan-constant SYSTEM prompt (cacheable, one per (shell, graph) pair), one per-unit INITIAL prompt (or one batch prompt), and the planner's system prompt + write_todos tool description. S4InvestigationProcedure renders, as control flow, the procedure these prompts ask the MODEL to carry out.

One agentic session per unit (or per batch of units): tool set, middleware (budgets, planner, evidence gate, model-call cap), dispatch with a deadline/resume/replay fallback, JSON repair, and reduction to findings.

S4 (deep-dive): every InvestigationUnit from S3 is investigated in its own agentic session (or a shared session for a batch of file-overlapping units). Returns (findings, outcome-per-unit) so a failed/blocked unit stays distinguishable from a clean one. The per-session wiring lives in s4/session.pseudo (S4Session).
Step 5: enrich S4's findings for S6 (snippet, evidence refs, sink re-anchor), refuse only coordinates that do not exist, trivially dedupe, then append zero-LLM detector rows.
S5's zero-LLM detector pass: run the shared detect/ rule corpus over every in-scope file, mint Findings from hits, dedupe against S4's kept findings, and cap the row count.
The fields S4 cannot produce (code snippet, sink/source refs), filled from the repo on disk.

What S5 still refuses: a coordinate that does not exist, and test-path noise. The S5 location knobs (re-anchor switch/cap, line tolerance) are listed here as the gate parameters; their real read site is s5/__init__.py run().
Deterministic sink-line re-anchor: a Python finding anchored on a function/class header is moved to the nearest in-scope sink call (own same-file sink_ref, else detect/ sink patterns for its CWE).
Path and weakness-class tables S5 matches against.
Step 6 package marker (batching, outcomes, prompts, session live in sibling modules).
Group findings into verification sessions (sorted by file), and compute the pool-sweep ceiling.
S6's output contract: one verdict per finding that can also CORRECT it (CWE, line, repeats, CVSS, trait stamps, discoveries). Field descriptions are prompt text; the reducer/router is code.

Agentic S6 prompts: one scan-constant SYSTEM prompt (role, verdicts, confidence, method, duties, exclusion rules A-F, CVSS, output example) and one per-batch VERIFY prompt; plus the JSON repair re-ask.
One agentic verification session per batch: tools and middleware (graph tools, tool budget, evidence gate, model-call budget), dispatch under a deadline with resume/replay, and a JSON repair.

Step 6: adversarial verification in batched agentic sessions on a daemon pool; only TRUE_POSITIVE findings at or above the confidence gate continue to S7. Failed batches are split and retried; findings the verifier discovers are re-verified in a second wave.
Step 7 package: re-exports the collapse helpers, the output contract, the prompt and the session.
The deterministic half of step 7: collapse same-site duplicates with no model call, and attach collapsed members onto their canonical as extra call sites.
Step 7's output contract (field descriptions the model reads as instructions) and the parse that fails open (an unparseable reply collapses nothing).

Step 7's prompt: the collapse test (SYSTEM) and the finding rows it rules on (build_payload). The model applies the collapse test to every unresolved finding; code refuses cross-CWE merges afterwards.
Step 7's one model call: the semantic dedup pass, degrading to no-collapse on any failure.
Step 7 deduplication: a deterministic same-site pass (also used by S5 as its prefilter), then one optional model call on the findings the deterministic pass could not resolve.
Step 8 package: rank verified findings by chaining opportunity and name the chains (re-exports).
Deterministic repo facts for the S8 prompt: redacted snippets (with decorator prologue), same-location groups, and deployment exposure (binds, published ports, Dockerfile USER).

Step 8's output contract (RankedEntry / ChainEntry / ChainReport field descriptions the model reads), the salvaging parse, the deterministic severity floor, and the reducer onto FinalReport with the chain gates (step validity, same-location collapse, link evidence, severity lift gate, dedup).
Step 8's prompts: the chaining brief (SYSTEM), the per-finding block it ranks, the repo fact blocks, the user prompt with EVIDENCE RULES, and the json-repair re-ask.
Step 8's one model call: the chaining pass (no tools, one model call), with a transcript replay on deadline and a json-repair re-ask; raises so S8Chain.run can ship the deterministic report.
Deterministic chain checks for S8: one-code-fact collapse, citation resolution, link coverage, hardening steps, quality annotations, the severity lift gate, chain dedup, unpromoted links.
Limits the S8 enrichment call to a deterministic rank prefix of findings (prompt-token and output-entry budgets) plus a one-pass same-file pull-in of MEDIUM/LOW/INFO hops.
Step 8: deterministic ranking floor plus model-optional chain/narrative enrichment over a rank-prefix window; any enrichment failure still ships the deterministically ranked report.
Step 9 package: render the final report to SARIF and stamp each result with its case id.
Builds S9's scan-health block (degradation facts) stamped onto the SARIF run invocation.
SARIF 2.1.0 emitter: one result per surviving finding, the duplicate-result guard, rules/taxa tables, run properties and scan-health notifications.
Step 9: emit the scan's SARIF document for the ingest hub and the IDE.
Namespace for optional graph/harness plugins.
Re-exports plugin/version, config/findings errors, enricher, findings readers, four tool factories/names and triage specialist.

One bounded Semgrep process enriches the structural graph with coverage, rule, finding and trace nodes. Subprocess/report failures degrade to a coverage node. Graph-construction exceptions are not caught by enrich().
Normalize bounded Semgrep JSON into ordinary Finding records before S5. Parsing/type errors not explicitly caught below propagate to the caller.
Graph enricher, read-only tools and triage-agent contribution; local files are validated before use.
Four read-only closures over the Semgrep subgraph; Cypher failures return error rows. Query LIMITs are embedded in the queries, not enforced by the unused _MAX_ROWS/_MAX_TRACE_STEPS constants.
Builds a specialist definition in CODE; the triage procedure and evidence gates are MODEL instructions.
Package facade for S10 remediation: re-exports discovery, interactive picker, options, runner, report parser and selection.
Renders and persists one remediation attempt to disk (re-export facade for layout/summary/diff/report/writer).
Scoped diff of the edited files: real git diff when possible, else a synthesized unified diff from a pre-edit snapshot (facade).
Picks between git diff and the synthesized fallback, so the diff is the harness's account, not the engine's.
Real git diff capture: a scoped diff for a file set (against a throwaway index copy, pre-edit baseline when given), plus the unscoped whole-tree changed set used by the post-gate as ground truth.
Repo-relative path normalisation and repo confinement (CWE-22) shared by every diff artifact and by revert.
Captures file contents before the agent edits them (for diff synthesis and post-gate restore), and which files changed since.
Synthesized git-style unified diff (difflib) from a pre-edit snapshot, for non-git targets. Never raises.
Per-finding artefact file names: single source of truth for writer, case builder and tests.
Assembles the canonical finding_case.json by joining the scan finding with the attempt this pass produced.
Human-readable per-finding summary.md renderer.

Persists one remediation attempt: finding_case.json at the root plus evidence/ (triage.json, summary.md, diff.patch), with secrets redacted at persistence; the diff is masked hunk-by-hunk preserving diff framing and line endings.
Locate the newest scan report, load findings (typed findings.json first, legacy Markdown fallback), mark already-remediated cases done, select top-N by CVSS and resolve the per-repo output layout.
Per-file language (from the finding's own extension) and per-repo framework detection: the keys the playbook resolves a strategy on.
Arrow-key issue picker for "vvaharness remediate -i", with a numbered-prompt fallback off a TTY (re-export facade).
Dependency-free terminal key input: decode a raw key sequence to UP/DOWN/ENTER/QUIT/OTHER and read one raw keypress.

Interactive remediation loops: arrow-key TUI on a real terminal, else a numbered prompt; both remediate one chosen finding at a time through remediateOne (never raises; a failure only fails that finding).
Menu rendering plus numbered-prompt selection parsing (1,3-5 | all | pending | q) for the interactive picker.
The structured-output contract for one remediation (re-export facade for change, fixer, gates, verdict).
One edited-file record in a remediation verdict.
Structured result returned by the S10 file-editor (fixer) subagent, with validators that tie success/retry claims to evidence.
The 3-gate evidence status block (source, sink, missing-control) as a reusable sub-model of the verdict.
The per-finding RemediationVerdict contract (frozen prompt schema), its salvage-not-raise coercion, and the translation to the shared RemediationEvidence contract.
Parse the remediate command's CLI flags (--resume, --interactive/-i, --verbose/-v, --mode, --top).
Fix-strategy resolver: the agent selects a strategy from the shipped playbook rather than inventing one. Resolution: CWE -> language -> framework -> default -> CWE fallback -> none.

FixerDispatchGuard: executor-side middleware on the orchestrator's "task" tool. It validates every fixer dispatch (subagent type, 4 ordered non-empty sections, primary file named), appends the authoritative finding context, and bounds attempts: one retry only after a transient tool error, one corrected re-dispatch after a malformed spec.
--verbose stderr tracing helpers: redacted labelled blocks and the per-finding policy decision. Pure presentation.
Wires the deterministic gate + playbook into the agent: a pre-gate before the LLM, a post-gate after (re-export facade).

Fail-closed regex scan of the lines an S10 patch ADDED (CWE-1427): rejects backdoors, dynamic code execution, network egress, credential reads and reverse shells that path gates and the agent's self-report cannot see.
Roll back forbidden-path edits on disk, confined to the repo: restore from the pre-edit snapshot, else git checkout (tracked) or delete (untracked, agent-created). Best-effort, never raises.

Pre-dispatch detection of symlinks escaping the scanned repo (CWE-59). An edit THROUGH an escaping link is invisible to the post-gate, so it is caught before the model gets a writer. Read-only and total: this reports, the caller refuses.

Fail-closed validation of S10 edits to reusable GitHub workflow refs ("uses: org/repo/.github/workflows/x.yml@ref"): a newly introduced ref must be a full, non-placeholder commit SHA already present in the pre-edit snapshot.
Deterministic eligibility gate facade: the only place deciding whether a finding reaches the patch agent.

Deterministic eligibility gate (pre-gate, before any model call) and the post-gate that reverts forbidden edits. Evaluation order: kill_switch -> deny -> deny_paths -> allow -> default_action. Missing/invalid policy fails closed.

S10 prompt text: single-agent SYSTEM (3 evidence gates, minimal-diff fix, structured verdict), the FIXER subagent prompt, the deepagents ORCHESTRATOR prompt (plan, dispatch fixer, collect), and the per-finding user prompt with policy/strategy blocks.

Trust boundary for S11: which on-disk finding cases this machine's S10 run actually produced. The repo-local security-remediation/ dir is untrusted; only checkpoint rows in the out-of-repo state store count.

S10 entry: parse the scan report, select the top-N findings by CVSS, and walk them through the per-finding fix loop. Also renders where the step_remediate.* session knobs take effect (policy context build, per-finding session invoke).

Renders one typed Finding as the "### N. [SEV] title" markdown block embedded in the remediation prompt. Model/repo-supplied prose is heading-demoted and snippets get a safe fence so they cannot forge prompt structure.
Locate the remediation rule files (policy + playbook) across source checkout, installed share dir and a user-configured inputs dir.

S10 per-finding loop: resume-or-run each finding sequentially, checkpoint the result, then augment the reports. apply_plugin wraps each session in the policy pre-gate, a file snapshot, and the harness post-gate/amend.
Facade for the shared "top N by CVSS" selection (pq.py + topspec.py), used by both remediation entry points.
Resolve the --top N cap (CLI flag wins over step_remediate.top_n_findings) and select the top N findings by CVSS.
One finding queued for remediation: wraps a scan Finding with its run index and the interactive "done" flag.
Report namespace; no runtime procedure.

Application context -> contextual severity: CMDB CSV loading with parent inheritance, an environmental CVSS 3.1 score (VulContextSeverity, "vsvs") from the app's data sensitivity and exposure, and the keyword-driven OffensivePriority (P1..P4) each verified finding carries.

CVSS 3.1 calculator (FIRST.org spec section 7): base score from a vector, sentinel variant, severity rating. The single home for the metric weights and formula coefficients (appcontext reuses them for environmental scoring).
Report-side CWE helpers: CWE id -> canonical MITRE name (unknown -> ""), the VulnClass -> CWE fallback used when a finding has no CWE, and the "CWE-NNN - Name" label renderers print.

Sensitive-data redaction applied at every write boundary (Markdown, SARIF, findings.json, error logs): ordered regex rules for card data, PII and credentials, each with a validator, plus a run-scoped value-carry registry that masks later restatements of an already-masked secret.

CweKB: in-memory, merge-on-load per-CWE taint knowledge (generic.kb.yaml plus optional overlays). Never raises into the pipeline: an unreadable pack degrades to empty. Served to S4/S6 via KbTools (for_cwes).
CWE id normalisation, weakness-class equivalence (used by S4 fan-out, S5/S7 collapse and S5 re-anchor), and the OWASP-2025 label map per sink family.

The generic CWE/OWASP starter knowledge base: per CWE, sources, sinks, sanitizers, non-sanitizers and FP checks. Served to S4/S6 sessions through the CweGuidance fact tool (KbTools) and the TAINT KB prompt block.
The CWE knowledge base as a fact tool (CweGuidance), composed into a session via compose_tool_builders.
Repo-kind classifier and its STRIDE-hint / minimum-baseline lookup tables for S2. Baseline ids BL-<kind>-<suffix> make the model's disposition machine-checkable (S2Baseline.audit).
Package facade: re-exports the deterministic repo walk, its exclusion sets and the config dedup. No logic of its own; each method delegates to the module that defines it.
S1 config dedup: collapses near-identical config files (same key-shape) to one representative per cluster, keeping any variant whose secret/insecure-value hits are not already in the representative.
The deterministic repo walk (every file S3/S4 may see), its built-in exclusion rules, agent-path normalisation against the inventory, and the secret/insecure-value regexes used by config dedup.

How skills reach a session: the packaged skill tree is copied into <repo>/.vvaharness/skills/ once per scan (S2/S4 hand it to the harness as skill_root), removed when the scan returns; the model picks a playbook by its description.

S4 skill playbook "access-control": IDOR/BOLA, missing authorization, privilege escalation, tenant isolation. The bug is usually an ABSENT check; hard gate = entry point + identity, and the object's ownership check.

S4 skill playbook "batch-etl": file-in -> transform -> file-out jobs; attacker is an upstream producer, scheduler parameter or shared landing directory. Hard gate = external value + unvalidated reach file:line.
S4 skill playbook "client-side": frontend lens. Nothing shipped to the client is secret; a client-only control is not a security control; the server line that trusts a client value is the finding.

Read-only client-side probe: inventory of client files and files of interest, lockfile check, then ~26 CWE-labelled grep sections (sinks, refutation evidence, server lines reading client params). Exits 0.

S4 skill playbook "code-exploration": the coverage procedure every lens runs on top of. Glob inventory -> directory census -> skipped file classes -> read to EOF -> follow edges -> FP checks -> enumerate -> coverage report.
Read-only probe the model may run: inventories file classes a source-only sweep skips, then runs escape / transport / CI / credential pattern batteries. Output-capped; always exits 0.

S4 skill playbook "crypto": weaknesses exploitable mathematically or by protocol negotiation, not generic hygiene. No HARD GATE section in this playbook; only a scope statement and a where-to-look list.
S4 skill playbook "csrf": state-changing endpoints a third-party origin can forge. Three-part hard gate, explicit-exemption exception, per-framework look list, one finding per handler. No probe.sh.

S4 skill playbook "deserialization": attacker-influenced bytes into code-invoking deserializers (JVM-centred). Hard gate = deserializer call site AND a path from untrusted input; both file:line points cited or drop.

S4 skill playbook "hardcoded-creds": literal credentials, keys, tokens and signing secrets committed to source. Settings/config files first, then source patterns; env-var references are never findings. No probe.sh.

S4 skill playbook "iac": Terraform / Docker / k8s / compose / CI / CloudFormation / Ansible misconfiguration. Probe inventory first, invert empty-means-absent sections, then judgement the grep cannot make.

Read-only IaC sweep: manifest inventory of seven platforms, then labelled known-bad / control-presence directive sections per platform plus cross-cutting TLS and credential literals. CAP=20 per section; exits 0.

S4 skill playbook "injection": every injection class in the description under a source/sink/no-defence hard gate. Probe first (probe.sh), refute candidates with the listed checks, then enumerate one finding per distinct sink.
Injection candidate sweep: one labelled grep section per injection class (CAP=20 hits shown), then a defence census. Run by the model through its shell tool; output is candidates only.
S4 skill playbook "log-injection": class A log injection (CWE-117), class B missing logging (CWE-778), class C plaintext credentials in logs (CWE-312/532), each with its own hard gate.
S4 skill playbook "logic-bug": behavioural / state-machine defects with no grep signature. Hard gate = trust-boundary citation (entry file:line + decision file:line); reason with seed questions.

S4 skill playbook "missing-controls": absent-control lens. Inverted method: enumerate every site a control belongs to, then judge site by site whether the control is on THIS path. One finding per absent site.

Read-only absent-control probe: (1) enumerate the sites each control belongs to, (2) where each control is actually present, (3) posture holes that are usually findings on sight. Capped per section; exits 0.

S4 skill playbook "sensitive-data": point-of-occurrence exposure (no injection path needed). Probe first, apply the sensitive-content + attacker-readable-channel gate, read polarity sections, then judgement checks.

Sensitive-data exposure sweep: ~20 labelled, case-insensitive grep sections across error/debug exposure, logging, serialization, storage, headers/caching, debug routes and settings constants; CAP=20 hits shown per section.

S4 skill playbook "sibling-instances": after a CONFIRMED weakness, sweep the whole repository for the same pattern, report one finding per confirmed site, check the same location for other classes, and state sweep counts.

S4 skill playbook "ssrf": outbound fetch whose destination derives from request-controlled input. Three-part gate, opaque-fetch-helper shape (the url PARAMETER is the sink), blind SSRF counts, one finding per sink site.

Read-only SSRF probe: fetch sinks in seven ecosystems, indirect mechanisms, url-parameter contracts and their call sites, request sources, allow-list/redirect posture, declared HTTP deps; reference tables only when a sink exists.

S4 skill playbook "templates": template/view-layer lens. A template file is a finding LOCATION; judge each interpolation by its output context; trace stored paths; info disclosure and CSRF at the same lines.

Read-only template/view probe: template inventory, layouts first, the whole sink battery across dialects, a per-<form> CSRF-token verdict, CSRF machinery, info disclosure, sanitizers, render sites, CSP. Exits 0.
Utility namespace; no runtime procedure.
One fail-safe reader for a dotted config knob, shared by every stage. Missing config, missing key and explicit null all read as the caller's default.
The product's human-facing output: status tables, glyph lines and the banner; diagnostics go to util.logs. Every printed value is redacted and stripped of terminal control characters first.

Process-wide stage counters (ints you add to, strings you overwrite), read once by util.metrics.build(). Batch mode must reset() between repos; retired tallies keep the whole batch invocation's totals.

Environment readiness engine shared by `vvaharness setup` and `vvaharness doctor`: interpreter, tools, agents, deps, credentials (presence only), tracing egress, TLS trust, config/backends. Preflight and scan reuse backendCredentialOk / gatewayCheck. A required FAIL blocks setup/doctor, not `scan`.
Structured error log shared across pipeline stages; one redacted JSON line per record. The orchestrator calls configure() once per scan; readers tally records per stage for reports/telemetry.
The catalogue of logged events: the member name is the stable code, the value is the sentence. Values carry no interpolation; data goes in log kwargs. Rendered as an enum (name, sentence).
Shared exception-chain walk plus the S2 hollow-threat-model stop exception.
The single answer to "is this path version-control metadata?" for every write gate.
Pull a JSON object/array out of a model response that may have prose or code fences around it. Candidate order: whole-fence body, every fenced block, then the raw text; first parseable span wins.
Structured logging for the vvaharness package: key-value lines to a terminal, JSON to a file, always redacted. Diagnostics only; nothing here changes what a scan finds.
Build ScanMetrics from pipeline state (units, outcomes, LOC, tokens, counters, errlog), kept out of the orchestrator; refresh_tokens re-snapshots token/cost/error fields after S8. Reporting only.
Host-literal predicates (spelling only, no DNS lookups), shared so copies cannot disagree.

Operator-supplied model price table (USD per Mtok by exact model id) used to cost a run's token counts. Must never fail a scan: any problem yields null costs. VVAHARNESS_PRICING_FILE overrides pricing.file.
Degenerate-response detector (VVAH-E003) for LLM replies, plus the shared failure classifiers (structured-output, truncation, timeout, connection, deterministic) and the retry-once-unforced wrapper.
Per-file / per-unit scan observability on stderr, gated on scan_progress.enabled, in one of six styles (compact, verbose, summary_only, stage_only, llm_debug, live). Never changes what a scan finds.
Process-wide per-stage telemetry (outcome, duration) and the composer of the run manifest's stages / totals / pricing sections: token phases are mapped to stages and costed per role model.
Per-stage status reporting on stderr (stdout stays clean for reports): start line or spinner, timed body, then a completion / completed-with-errors / incomplete / failed line, or JSON events.
Process-wide token accounting shared by every model backend (per-phase buckets), plus the one offline content-aware token estimator used to size prompts and windows.
One-shot stderr warnings: print a message at most once per key; each caller owns its seen set. _REGISTRY_SITES lists every module-level seen set so batch runs can clear them between repos.
Validation namespace; no runtime procedure.
S11 entry point for one in-memory case (SDK validate): stage a workspace, run the gate pipeline, score. Never writes to the target repo; the temp workspace is always removed.
Claude Code Stop hook in the S11 session: copies the raw (unredacted) session transcript into the logging dir, only when an operator opts in. Fail-open: every failure exits 0.

S11 rule file (auto-loaded from .claude/rules/ on Claude routes, inlined into the system prompt otherwise): persona isolation, anti-manipulation, synthesis rules, evidence requirements, secret-evidence handling, signal-to-noise.

S11 scoring rule file: four weighted gates, status multipliers, thresholds, critical gate, merge readiness, the 8-step algorithm the model is told to run, code-level-signals scope, and secret-exposure handling. ScoringEngine is the host twin.
Claude Code project settings injected into the S11 workspace (.claude/settings.json): session model, read-only tool permissions, and the Stop hook that captures the transcript.

S11 skill (injected into .claude/skills on Claude routes): condensed copy of the scoring matrix, isolation, anti-manipulation, code-level-signals and secret-exposure rules, plus the read-only output contract.
Trust and path preflight precede staging/spend; temporary workspaces are cleaned even on early failure.
Resolve panel model/transport and persona model IDs. Persona transport settings are advisory and ignored.
Argument parser for `vvaharness validate` (alias s11) and the step_validate tunables forwarded as typed overrides into the validation config layer.
Compiled regex used by the cli package to make ids filesystem-safe.
Sequential validation, state-store provenance and resume, case writeback and report augmentation. A refusal/session failure outranks verdicts when choosing the process exit code.
The parsed command line for `vvaharness validate` as a frozen record.
Validation agent configuration facade (the only place environment is read); re-exports the settings tree.
Profile-sourced tunables that seed load_config(); every absent key falls back to the shipped default, never to the VVAHARNESS_* environment.
Typed configuration tree package; re-exports AgentConfig, Config, GheConfig, PathsConfig, load_config.
Agent runtime knobs for S11: model selection, backend, execution limits (pydantic model, extra=forbid).
The composed S11 configuration tree and load_config(), which fills it from profile overrides or hard-coded defaults (never from the environment, except credentials/binary).
The flat VVAHARNESS_* environment surface: only the claude binary and the GHE tokens are read.
GitHub Enterprise tokens passed through to the agent for gh api.
Filesystem layout for a validation run (targets/, outputs/ under the project root; prompts/ from the package).
Resolves the models.validate role from a harness profile, and reroutes a legacy via: openai role onto DeepAgents with the OpenAI provider.
Constants namespace; no runtime procedure.

Single source of truth for S11 artifact names, the validatable case states, files excluded from the staged workspace, env-key names, and the default agent runtime values (fallbacks of step_validate knobs).
Constants for the deterministic diff-based fact tools (hunk parsing, trust-boundary detection).
Immutable bundled validation-panel configuration.
Constants for the deterministic PatternScan fact tool: built-in pattern sets and scan skips.
Validation-specific tool policy: read-only allow-list for the orchestrator and the write gate.
Host-computed policy; prompt scoring instructions have independent copies of some values.
Host-panel agreement floor; low agreement or a tie flags the synthesized status.
Constants for the TestInventory fact tool: which files count as tests, and which markers make a test "negative".
Tool-name vocabularies for the validation agent: the deterministic fact tools and the DeepAgents default grant.
Engine-local enums for validation; EffortLevel, Provider and SettingSource are re-exported from backends.harness.
Confidence label attached to a host-synthesized persona-report consensus.
Execution package facade: re-exports execute_plan from execution/pipeline.py.
Execute one validation plan, collecting host-enriched verdicts. Expected session failures return an unscored result.
Per-CWE adversarial bypass hints package facade.
Loads per-CWE adversarial bypass hints from the operator-supplied inputs/validator_hints.yaml. No bundled fallback: absent file = no hints; malformed = warn and ignore.
Ingest layer facade: case discovery (case_loader), workspace staging, the applied-fix gate, and the manifest.
Discover safe case paths, enforce provenance before filtering or CVSS caps, and preserve explicit ID order.
Ingest-layer error: any defensive ingest refusal (missing case, or an unapplied fix).
Builds the agent-facing single-finding manifest for one case.
Stages a pre-patched by-value copy of the target repo for S11 (excluding VCS/build dirs, agent-instruction files and escaping symlinks), and refuses validation when no touched file of the fix exists.
Validation I/O namespace; no runtime procedure.
Deterministic host-side scoring from synthesized_gates.json; the agent's own score/fix_status is never authoritative. Fails closed: absent or malformed gates -> INCONCLUSIVE with no score.
Builds a case's verdict from workspace artifacts (agent report narrative + host-scored gates) and writes it back onto the case's latest attempt.
Drains a Harness streaming session to session.jsonl (one JSON line per message), prints optional live previews, and derives the exit status from the terminal HarnessResult.
Pulls persona reports out of the session's terminal state: pre-parsed SDK/CLI reports, or JSON ToolMessages in the DeepAgents graph state. Validates and dedupes them.
Collects fix-validation verdicts from validation_report.json, re-scored host-side from synthesized gates, and renders report rows, filling blank row fields from manifest.json.
Engine-local data shapes facade for the validation agent; re-exports manifest, output, persona report, plans, results (gate_score_rows, render_row, unverifiable_row) and scoring models.
Per-finding workspace manifest for the agent session (extra keys ignored); carries the Finding whole.

Strict (frozen) structured-output schema of the S11 session: per-finding blocks and synthesized gates. Validators coerce/redact/truncate CSV fields, clamp raw_score, and redact narrative text on load.
Wire shapes for persona reports (frozen). Extra keys ignored; an unknown gate status fails closed to INVALID.
Execution-plan value object for validating one pre-staged finding.
Per-run counters and the flat render row the S11 report builds from (a render row, not a contract).
Value types shared by the scoring engine: raw criteria, verdict bands, score results and ScoringConfig, which converts to/from the host ScoringPolicy (policy thresholds become decision bands).

S11 orchestrator system prompt: read-only lead that dispatches three adversarial personas in parallel, waits for exactly three PersonaReports, and returns one ValidationOutput. Synthesis/Rules sections are appended by the launcher.
Combined-report augmentation facade: writes S11 validation results into the SARIF + MD report.

Best-effort augmentation of the combined SARIF + Markdown report with S11 results; never fails the run. SARIF: match each finding to a result (fingerprint, then location, then unique title) and attach a properties.validation block (resultIdentifies/resultFingerprint/recordResultBlock are imported from pipeline/stages/s9/typed_sarif.py). MD: replace/append a "### Validation" section under each matc
Data shapes for combined-report augmentation.
Public host scoring API: parse raw gate dicts, score them with the engine against a policy, and return a typed ValidationScore (decision, raw score, gates, critical-failure flag).
The fix-validation ScoringConfig, derived from the engine's FIX_POLICY (gates, weights, critical gates, bands).
Deterministic scoring: fail closed before scoring; skipped gates leave the denominator. Conversion to GateStatus can raise. Parsing is not itself a catch-all validation boundary.

Fix-path justification builder: the host's tracker-comment text per decision (Fixed / Partial / Not Fixed), citing gate summaries, a 0-100 confidence and evidence anchors. INCONCLUSIVE is not re-narrated.
Validation session package facade: config injection, error type, launch prompt, launcher.

Injects the .claude/ runtime config (rules, optional skills, transcript hook, settings.json) into a validation workspace for Claude-Code-backed sessions. The scoring package is deliberately not copied.
Per-session failure that drives a case INCONCLUSIVE; wraps the harness error and renders a diagnostic.
S11 launch (user) prompt for one fix-validation session: case/session header, patch-under-validation guidance, finding details with bypass hints, and the session config / post markers.

Launch one isolated validation session, meter and log its stream, refuse failed/refused output before writing verdicts. The host owns deterministic synthesis only on backends returning validated persona reports.

Reads the bundled validation rules as prompt text (licence comment stripped) for backends that do not load .claude/rules natively: the orchestrator gets both rules files, each persona the adversarial one.
Validation-specific values injected into the shared harness: skill root, write gate, tool policy, fact-tool grant, output schema and the DeepAgents validation tools.
Bundled subagent definitions facade: re-exports load_agents from subagents/_loader.py.
Strict mini-YAML frontmatter parser for subagent .md files: only known scalar keys and block-list keys; any other key or a malformed line is a hard error.
Loads the three isolated validation personas from their bundled .md files (frontmatter + body prompt), applies the tool override, prompt suffix and per-persona model-call cap.
Parse bundled persona files; an override narrows declared tools and preserves declared fact tools.

S11 persona subagent: always-on completeness and regression auditor; re-derives the vulnerability scope by repo-wide search and never defaults a gate to skip. Output and anti-manipulation text is shared with the other personas.
Data shapes for parsed subagent YAML frontmatter.

S11 persona subagent: penetration tester judging real-world exploitability and production failure modes of the fix; returns one PersonaReport. Criterion-evaluation, output and anti-manipulation text is identical to security-architect.md.
S11 persona subagent: security architect judging fix design, data flow and coverage; returns one PersonaReport with a qualitative status per gate (no score, no synthesis).
Consensus namespace; no runtime procedure.

Deterministic host synthesis of the three persona gate reports into one gate status per gate. 2+ agreeing votes (unique top) win at HIGH confidence; otherwise the most conservative top status wins, FLAGGED.
Fact tools namespace; no runtime procedure.

Shared in-scope file iteration for the validation fact tools: mirrors the S1 production scan scope (module defaults, not the run's config), optionally keeps test dirs, and refuses workspace-escaping symlinks.
DeepAgents tool-builder for S11: the generic reader tools plus each deterministic fact tool whose name is in the allow-list.
